context.guidance: Do not write Personal Data or Authentication Secrets to localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies or outbound headers beyond what the session strictly needs. Keep identity in an opaque session identifier held server-side, and keep only non-Personal Data preferences in the browser. Where a value must be held client-side, protect it as Rule 6(1)(a) requires.

value.fix: Remove the `localStorage.setItem('email', user.email)` call. Email is Personal Data, and localStorage persists it across sessions and exposes it to any script running on the origin, including XSS. Keep identity on the server: after login, store the user's identity in a server-side session and send the browser only an opaque, random session ID in an `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` (or `Lax`) cookie. When the UI needs the user's email, fetch it from an authenticated endpoint (e.g. `GET /api/me`) that reads the identity from the server-side session, and hold the value only in in-memory component state so it is discarded on reload or logout. Delete any existing `localStorage.getItem('email')` reads and clear any previously stored `email` key on logout (`localStorage.removeItem('email')`) to remove legacy copies. Only non-Personal Data preferences, such as theme or language, may remain in browser storage. Verify the fix by confirming that after login `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` contain no email, that the cookie is opaque and flagged `HttpOnly`/`Secure`, and that `/api/me` returns the email only with a valid session.
